ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) PEP list, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, Her Majesty's Treasury consolidated list, and New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs sanctions lists. Required for all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and senior management. Enhanced due diligence applies to higher-risk jurisdictions and complex ownership structures. Ongoing review required at least annually and upon triggering events.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_and_aml_profiling_pretty_print: UBO disclosure level is Government-Only Access. Threshold is 25% ownership or control. Verification requires notarized ID, apostille/consular legalization, and screening against PEP and sanctions lists.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz/companies) administered by the New Zealand Companies Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use English or Māori words using the Latin script; non-Latin scripts may be used only in parentheses or as a supplementary name. Names must be distinguishable from existing registered names, not misleading, and comply with s 25 of the Companies Act 1993 (availability, no restricted words, no deceptive connotation).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name approval is refused, the applicant may submit a formal objection/reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies within 15 working days, providing evidence of non-conformance or distinctiveness. If rejection persists, the applicant may file for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 / Senior Courts Act 2016. Alternatively, the applicant may amend and reapply through the Companies Office online portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office may be accepted for low-risk administrative functions, but for a vertical ERP/CRM cloud software entity, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and Companies Office expect a physical commercial substance presence (e.g. domain-specific operational capability) in New Zealand if claiming local tax residency or treaty benefits. A 'mere virtual office' without any real substance may trigger anti-avoidance scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (approx. 30-45%) within the first two years of operation, especially if GST refunds, cross-border invoices, or treaty relief claims are lodged; cloud software businesses with low physical footprint may attract targeted verification reviews.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), in particular sections 12–19 (Registration of Companies), 126–136 (Share Capital), 152 (Requirement for at least one Director Resident in New Zealand or an Australian Resident Director), 189 (Registered Office), 190 (Address for Service) and the Companies (Companies Register) Regulations 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Te Rārangi Inihua), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), administered electronically through the Companies Register portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Incorporation Application (NZCN1 equivalent) submitted via the Companies Register RealMe portal, accompanied by Consent to Act as Director and any adopted Constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; New Zealand law requires only the issue of at least one scanned share at par value. No escrow bank account or capital deposit is required. The Company must maintain a registered office and an address for service in New Zealand, and, if the Company has a physical presence in New Zealand, at least one director must be resident in New Zealand (or be a director resident in Australia who has his or her principal residence in Australia and is also a director of a New Zealand company). Non-resident ownership is unrestricted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED DATED __________ 20___

RESOLVED, that the allotment and issue of ordinary shares in the share capital of the Company, as recorded in the register of shareholders and in the Application for Shares, be and is hereby approved and confirmed, and that the initial subscription consideration be applied for the lawful purposes of the Company.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby adopted at [Street Address], New Zealand, and that the said address be filed as the registered office under section 189 of the Companies Act 1993 and as the address for service under section 190 thereof.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as the sole director of the Company, to hold office until otherwise determined in accordance with the Company’s constitution and the Companies Act 1993, and that the director be and is hereby authorized to open and operate bank accounts, execute contracts, engage solicitors, accountants, and auditors, and take all actions necessary to register the Company with the New Zealand Companies Office and the Inland Revenue Department.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that execution of any borrowing, guarantee, or security arrangements consistent with the Company’s business be and is hereby delegated to the director.

CERTIFIED by the subscriber on this ______ day of ________________, 20___.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name search, availability check, and optional name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – online name search and reservation facility on the Companies Register portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a free name availability search on the Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name and does not contain a restricted word. If a distinctive name is identified and immediate incorporation is not intended, submit an optional online application to reserve the name for 20 working days, paying the NZD 25 (approx. USD 16) reservation fee. Otherwise proceed directly to the online incorporation application using the same name.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (up to 5 alternatives recommended)
RealMe login credentials for the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity to an existing name or for contravening the requirements of section 22 of the Companies Act 1993, submit a new distinctive name or obtain a letter of consent from the holder of the existing name. Objections can be resolved by correspondence with the Companies Office before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of constitutional and governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office guidance and the company's appointed legal advisor or chartered accountant (pre-submission preparation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft or adopt the Company's constitution (either the 'Companies Act 1993 First Schedule' default constitution or a custom constitution) and prepare the shareholder register, consent to act as director, and the first board resolution. Confirm the identity and residency of the initial shareholder(s) and director(s). For a tax-exempt non-resident 'International Company' intended to be managed and controlled outside New Zealand, record the place of effective management (POEM) outside New Zealand for informational support of the tax status. Verify that the director satisfies section 152 of the Companies Act 1993 (natural person age 18+ and, if the Company pursues an in-country physical presence, an NZ resident director).
required_dossiers: Draft or adopted Constitution (if any)
Consent to Act as Director signed by each proposed director
Certified copy of each director's passport and proof of address
Declaration of principal place of business / POEM outside New Zealand
First Board Resolution (pro forma above) signed by the initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar subsequently queries governance provisions, amend the constitution by special resolution of the shareholders and file an updated notice with the Companies Office. Incomplete director consent forms are rejected; obtain a fresh signature and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Online Incorporation Application (NZCN1) and payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register electronic incorporation portal (RealMe authenticated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Companies Register and select 'Register a Company'. Enter the approved company name, the proposed registered office address in New Zealand (must physically exist and be open to the public), the address for service, the full legal name, birth date, and residential address of each director, the full name and address of the shareholder, and the number and class of shares to be issued. Tick the declaration that all persons consent to act. Upload the signed consent forms and any adopted constitution. Review and submit the application, then pay the NZD 150 (approx. USD 95) incorporation fee by debit/credit card or online banking. The system instantaneously generates a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Completed NZCN1 online application form
Signed Consent to Act as Director for each director
Constitution (if custom constitutional provisions are used)
Notice of registered office and address for service in New Zealand
First shareholder return / initial shareholding details
Payment of NZD 150 fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or rejection under sections 13–17 of the Companies Act 1993 (e.g., incorrectly completed consent, non-qualifying registered office address, or objectionable name), correct the flagged fields online and resubmit within the statutory correction window. Contact the Companies Office helpdesk for expedited resolution; the application is typically assessed within one working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, and company extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Companies Office electronically issues the Certificate of Incorporation confirming the company's legal existence from the date of registration. The corresponding New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) is auto-assigned. Download the official company extract and incorporation certificate from the Companies Register, which will be used for bank account opening and ongoing compliance.
required_dossiers: No additional dossiers – issued automatically from the approved application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation is not generated or is defective, request a certified reissue from the Registrar by filing a 'Notice of Correction' or by contacting the Companies Office customer service. Corrections are processed without additional fee within one working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation corporate registers, offices, and first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – company records and the Company's registered office / company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the statutory registers (register of shareholders, register of directors, register of charges) and file any required notices of interest with the Companies Office. Update the registered office with evidence of the physical New Zealand address and notify the Companies Office if the registered office provider is a licensed agent. Hold the first board meeting to formally adopt the first board resolution, approve the share issuance, designate the bank signatories, authorize the opening of bank accounts and payment gateway accounts (Stripe Billing / Direct Debit through a New Zealand acquiring bank), and appoint the company secretary or corporate service provider if desired.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Share register and application forms
First Board Resolution and board minutes
Letter from the registered office service provider
Bank and payment gateway application forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office records are incomplete or a notice of charge is not filed, file a corrective notice (Form NZCN3 or NZCN4 as applicable) together with the supporting declaration. Late filing corrections incur a standard late filing fee and can be remedied by online submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Inland Revenue (IRD number) and confirmation of non-resident tax exempt status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand and the New Zealand Companies Office (for tax registration linkage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the Inland Revenue Department using the IRD registration portal (or via the Companies Office integrated registration). Submit an IR596 declaration confirming the company is managed and controlled outside New Zealand and has no New Zealand-sourced income, thus qualifying as a non-resident 'tax-exempt' company for NZ purposes. If the company later opens a New Zealand physical office or hires employees, it must instead register for employer obligations (PAYE, ACC) and GST (if turnover exceeds NZD 60,000). For the purely non-resident software-as-a-service business model with payment rails of Stripe Billing and Direct Debit, no GST registration is required unless the company enters into GST-taxable transactions in New Zealand.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
IR596 non-resident company declaration
Evidence of POEM outside New Zealand (shareholder and board minutes)
Bank account details for any refund or tax credit, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD assesses the company as a New Zealand resident for tax purposes, provide comprehensive evidence of POEM outside New Zealand, apply for a binding ruling, and if necessary restructure the directorship so that central management and control are exercised offshore. An accountant may request a 'Notice of Response' and a determination under the double tax agreement procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ongoing annual compliance and corporate governance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and Inland Revenue Department (if tax registered)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual return (Annual Return) with the Companies Office on the company's registration anniversary and deliver any changes in director details, registered office, or shareholding via the online portal. Maintain the company registers and minute books. As the company is a 'tax-exempt zone' non-resident entity, there is no in-country tax return requirement, except for withholding tax on any NZ-source dividends, interest, or royalties, which are handled at bank-source level.
required_dossiers: Annual return confirmation online
Updated register of directors, shareholders, and charges
Notice of any change in directors (NZ1CN9 equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a late filing penalty is imposed by the Companies Office, apply for an extension under the late filing remission policy or file promptly with a written explanation of the default; correction requests are handled on a case-by-case basis.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – vertical industrial ERP/CRM software development is classified under ISIC 6201 (Computer programming activities) and ANZSIC 7000/5411; no industrial license or operating authorization is required by the Companies Act 1993, the Commerce Act 1986, or the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for the provision of cloud-based software. The competent authority for any incidental importation of hardware would be the New Zealand Customs Service (NZCS), and for intellectual property rights, the Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand (IPONZ).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operational or manufacturing permit required for pure software/cloud activities. If the company establishes a physical office in New Zealand, a standard Building Warrant of Fitness is required under the Building Act 2004 for commercial premises, and a Fire Evacuation Scheme approved by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) must be lodged.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical production facility or land-based activity is conducted; the software-as-a-service business is not listed under Schedule 1 of the Resource Management Act 1991 or the Exclusive Economic Zone and Continental Shelf (Environmental Impact – Permitted Activities) Regulations 2013. Therefore no EIA or resource consent is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – the Company has no wastewater, VOC, or solid waste discharge streams. If the Company were to operate physical data centers or office premises, the relevant thresholds are the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ) under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the Building Act 2004 energy efficiency and internal air quality standards, none of which bind a remote software enterprise.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for the pure cloud-delivered software business. Conditionally, if the Company later opens a New Zealand office, the following clearances would be required: (a) a Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire safety certificate or an approved evacuation scheme for premises with more than 10 people or a total floor area exceeding 100 m²; (b) a structural building warrant of fitness under the Building Act 2004 for the premises; (c) a workplace health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including an Injury Prevention Plan; and (d) if operating a data center, compliance with the Electrical Regulations (Wiring) 2010. As the company has no in-country physical employees, no occupational trade license is mandated.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand Government; taxpayer portal: myIR (www.ird.govt.nz); company registry: New Zealand Companies Office (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) through the New Zealand Companies Office, then apply for an IRD number for non-resident companies using form IR742 or online via a myIR account. The application requires certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, director and ultimate beneficial owner details, registered office address, and a physical address in the home jurisdiction. No statutory minimum capital is required, and non-resident ownership is permitted without a local director mandate for foreign companies carrying on business in New Zealand (a local agent for service may be required). GST registration is a separate application under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, requiring a New Zealand contact person or agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style Check-the-Box regime and does not provide pass-through elections for corporate entities. Hybrid mismatch rules enacted under BEPS (Income Tax Act 2007, sections FH 6–FH 14) deny deductions for hybrid financial instrument arrangements and imported mismatches, but contain limited ordering and opt-in elections for deemed deductions. A non-resident company may elect to be treated as a New Zealand resident for tax purposes under the tie-breaker provisions of a double tax agreement, and a transitional resident may elect for the four-year exemption from most foreign income. For GST, a non-resident supplier making supplies below the NZD 60,000 threshold may elect voluntary registration to claim input tax credits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — New Zealand value-added tax system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in New Zealand in any 12-month period (including remote services and low-value goods supplied by offshore suppliers into New Zealand)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate exists. New Zealand adopts the Peppol framework for voluntary B2B e-invoicing through accredited access points and service providers; IRD accepts electronic invoices provided they contain the statutory GST invoice fields and are retained in a readable format. GST returns and invoice summaries are submitted periodically via myIR or approved gateway software, not per-invoice real-time APIs.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (i) supplies of goods physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the supply (or under an approved export procedure); (ii) supplies of services to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, where the services are supplied for use and enjoyment outside New Zealand, including offshore cloud/ERP/CRM subscription services delivered remotely; (iii) international freight and transport services; and (iv) certain business-to-business remote services supplied to a non-resident GST-registered recipient, subject to the 'land-connected' exception denying zero-rating for services directly connected with New Zealand land or goods. The supplier must hold reasonable evidence of exportation and of the recipient's non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (T2) or New Zealand Customs Service export entry / electronic export manifest
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other shipping delivery evidence showing physical export from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/foreign currency transfer evidence of payment received from the non-resident customer
Commercial invoice, GST invoice, and proof of service delivery or cloud usage location outside New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD may reassess and claw back improperly claimed zero-rating within the four-year GST adjustment period, extended indefinitely in cases of fraud or wilful misrepresentation. Penalties include use-of-money interest on unpaid tax, shortfall penalties of 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or fraudulent intent. Export zero-rating fraud may additionally trigger criminal prosecution, director personal liability, and compulsory GST deregistration. Substantiation documents must be retained for seven years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) as the central bank and sole monetary and FX policy authority; Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as the conduct regulator for financial service providers; Overseas Investment Office (OIO) within Land Information New Zealand for foreign investment screening; Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Authority (FISA) as the licensing and supervisory authority for the Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) and its registered agents. No separate foreign-exchange-control administration exists in New Zealand; exchange controls are effectively nil under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 and OECD liberalisation commitments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. The NZD is freely floating with no central bank exchange-rate band, no approval requirement for inward or outward remittances, and no restriction on profit repatriation. For the CK_IC (Tax_Exempt_Zone model): pure offshore ERP/CRM subscription revenue from non-NZ customers incurs zero New Zealand exchange or tax friction; any NZ-source income attributable to a permanent establishment would be subject to New Zealand corporate income tax at 28%, after which after-tax profits may be remitted freely, subject to non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at the default 30% for dividends and 15% for royalties/interest under applicable double-tax agreements. Practical hurdles are limited to AML/CFT documentary evidence, thin-capitalisation / transfer-pricing documentation where the CK_IC capitalises an NZ subsidiary or branch, and the absence of any restriction on holding NZD or foreign-currency accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation exists in New Zealand. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0% and there is no statutory timeline for repatriation; exporters may indefinitely retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds in onshore Foreign Currency Accounts or offshore accounts. No reporting to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand is required, though transactional records must be retained for a minimum of five years under the AML/CFT Act 2009. For the CK_IC as global exporter of ISIC 6201 vertical CRM software, USD, EUR, AUD and NZD subscription income may remain un-converted in a multi-currency treasury ledger and converted at the desired commercial rate in accordance with the treasury hedging policy.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational Multi-Currency Account
Operational NZD/USD Account; Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with FX Hedging Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility for the CK_IC software exporter: High, subject to three legal constraints. (1) Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Payoneer, Revolut) are permissible as inbound collection and outbound disbursement rails without a New Zealand FSP licence, provided the EMI does not carry on business in New Zealand under s.5 of the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; the CK_IC may maintain an offshore EMI account outside New Zealand. (2) Direct Debit (BECS) origination requires an NZ clearing-bank sponsor; consequently, the Direct_Debit payment rail must be operated through a licensed NZ bank or a licensed payment aggregator such as Stripe Billing with an NZ acquiring bank, and cannot be executed by an offshore EMI acting alone. (3) AML/CFT Act 2009 obligations arise at the point of collection from NZ-domiciled customers; the merchant-of-record structure under Stripe Billing must clearly identify the CK_IC, and the EMI's KYC file must cover the full UBO chain. Overall rating: High for cross-border subscription collections and low-value disbursements; Medium for NZD-denominated local clearing absent an NZ bank co-sponsor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory mandate: none. The AML/CFT Act 2009 permits risk-based remote customer due diligence. For this Low_Risk_Standard ISIC 6201 entity, Tier-1 New Zealand banks will generally allow fully remote onboarding via video-call identity verification plus a DIA-Trusted Identity Provider, conditional on the CK_IC supplying: (i) the notarised Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing from the Cook Islands Registrar/FISA; (ii) a certified board resolution authorising the New Zealand banking relationship; (iii) an executed New Zealand registered-agent and physical-address agreement; (iv) identification of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners (passport and proof of residential address); and (v) W-8BEN-E or CRS tax self-certifications. Where a trust is the UBO, the trustee must present by video link with a trust-deed extract. In practice, ANZ and Westpac accept video identification for FATF-equivalent jurisdictions; physical appearance becomes a de facto requirement only if the entity lacks any New Zealand nexus (no agent, no GST registration, no local contract).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: incorporation in a low-tax offshore jurisdiction (Cook Islands IC) without visible commercial substance in New Zealand
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing under the Cook Islands International Companies Act 2012; economic-substance declaration evidencing direction and management in the Cook Islands or a treaty-compliant alternate jurisdiction; board minutes authorising the New Zealand banking relationship; executed SaaS/ERP customer contracts under ISIC 6201; FISA annual maintenance fee receipt; current offshore tax-exempt status letter; registered-agent confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: opaque UBO chain via trust or nominee shareholders triggers enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership register under the IC Act 2012; UBO declaration forms (name, DOB, nationality, residential address, ownership percentage); trust-deed extract identifying immediate and ultimate beneficiaries if a trust owns the CK_IC; signed trustee resolutions confirming the legal-and-beneficial ownership split; FATCA/CRS tax self-certifications for each UBO; independent legal opinion confirming no bearer shares or nominee ambiguity; cancellation certificate if bearer shares have been eliminated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: source-of-funds / source-of-wealth mismatch for the capital escrow injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share-subscription agreement and board allotment resolution; historical bank statements from the funding jurisdiction covering a 6-12 month period; contemporaneous sale-and-purchase agreement and independent IP valuation where the capital injection is made by contributing ERP/CRM software intellectual property; statutory declaration attesting to the origin of funds; reference letter from the transferring Cook Islands licensed bank; complete audit trail demonstrating that no unrelated third-party funds pass through the escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Stripe Billing / Direct Debit collection pattern indicates possible money-service-business (MSB) or merchant-of-record arbitrage
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete Stripe merchant agreement and settlement statements demonstrating itemised SaaS subscription nomenclature aligned with ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210; sample end-user licence agreements; written description of the vertical CRM/ERP business distinguishing it from remittance or payments processing; the entity's AML/CFT policy and staff training records; BECS Direct Debit user-authorisation records with clear debtor consent; GST registration certificate and filed returns; revenue-versus-disbursement reconciliation proving that no third-party funds other than business revenue pass through the accounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (A) equity injections must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 from the CK_IC's Cook Islands or offshore bank directly to the authorised New Zealand Tier-1 bank account, with the remitter field reading exactly 'CK_IC (Cook Islands International Company)' and the order-information field stating 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION – CAPITAL INJECTION CK_IC'; the OECD purpose code should be 'TRF' (general transfer) or 'NTR' (non-trade services) as required by the receiving bank, and the beneficiary account must be in the name of the CK_IC. (B) Pre-notify the New Zealand relationship manager with the certified board resolution, share allotment form, capital contribution agreement, Cook Islands tax-exempt certificate, and UBO declarations before the wire arrives. (C) If the injection is structured as a shareholder loan rather than equity, use purpose code 'LOAN' and provide a signed facility agreement to prevent misclassification as trading revenue. (D) Funds must never be aggregated, split, or sourced from unrelated third parties; only a single remitter connected to the UBO chain is acceptable. (E) Any conversion of USD/EUR to NZD must be executed at the bank's commercial rate or an agreed forward rate under FMA fair-dealing rules, with the conversion contract documented. (F) All records must be retained for a minimum of seven years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for all vendor, channel-partner, licence-fee, and infrastructure payments equal to or above NZD 25,000 (or foreign-currency equivalent), carrying invoice references and purpose codes such as 'SOFTWARE LICENSING FEE', 'HOSTING INFRASTRUCTURE LEASE', and 'OVERSEAS CONTRACTOR SERVICES'. (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits under UCP600) for hardware co-location or data-centre procurement where the counterparty requires payment security, issued by the NZ bank against a collateralised account balance. (3) BECS (Bulk Electronic Clearing System) Direct Debit and credit transfer for NZD-denominated local disbursements such as New Zealand cloud-backup providers, legal, and accounting services. (4) Stripe Payouts or Airwallex/Wise API transfers for low-value recurring contractor commissions below USD 2,000 per payment, with consolidated FX and reconciliation files. (5) For EU/UK beneficiaries, NZ banks route via SWIFT with BIC/IBAN; SEPA clearing is not directly accessible from New Zealand, so a multi-currency account held at an approved EMI node may net small euro-denominated payments. All outbound wires must attach the correct purpose code and invoice reference to ensure traceability and to satisfy the bank's transaction monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD, NZD/GBP)
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for USD/NZD matched capital and trade cash flows
Plain Vanilla FX Options and zero-cost collars (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) on restricted emerging-market currencies (e.g., KRW, INR, CLP) executed with OECD licensed banks
FX Swaps (spot-to-forward) for intra-quarter liquidity smoothing and multi-currency cash conversion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Company (Companies Act 1993, section 215)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the company's incorporation anniversary month; return due no later than one month after the anniversary return date as stated on the Companies Office reminder.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the statutory window exposes the company to removal from the New Zealand Companies Register under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993; directors may be prosecuted and fined, and reinstatement requires a court order and payment of the Registrar's reinstatement fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) and Financial Performance Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 March balance date, return due by 7 July; for non-standard balance dates, due within 7 months of the balance date. Terminal tax is due by 7 April for the standard balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: IRD late filing penalty NZD 250 per return; late payment penalties accrue (1% immediately and 4% after 7 days plus ongoing monthly escalation); interest is charged, and persistent non-filing may lead to prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Audited Financial Statements (required for companies meeting 'large' thresholds under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, or where shareholders require an audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies) if filed; Inland Revenue Department if submitted with the tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months of balance date for a large company (e.g., 31 August for a 31 March balance date) if financial statements are required to be filed with the Companies Office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and the company may be subject to infringement fees or criminal penalties for non-compliance with the Financial Reporting Act 2013; the Registrar may issue formal warnings and initiate prosecution for continued failure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory if the company is 'large' under section 45 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013: total assets exceed NZD 60 million (approx. USD 36 million) or total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million (approx. USD 18 million) in each of the two most recent consecutive accounting periods. A company below both thresholds is exempt unless shareholders require an audit or the company's constitution mandates one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS); small and medium-sized entities may adopt the NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime or the financial reporting framework appropriate to entity size.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no separate annual UBO confirmation filing for ordinary private companies; the company must maintain an up-to-date register of members and control interests and report a transfer of shares or a change in control to the Companies Office within 10 working days. Directors must ensure that annual return information on shareholders and control interests is accurate as of the anniversary date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Share Transfers
Register of Directors and Their Notices of Resignation
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Resolutions
Register of Charges (if any security interests granted)
